provider: AWS Lambda layers (and function deployment packages)

free_tier.stated: Per-function/per-layer caps only, plus a regional aggregate. Verbatim: 'Deployment package (.zip file archive) size | 50 MB (zipped, when uploaded through the Lambda API or SDKs) ... 50 MB (when uploaded through the Lambda console) ... 250 MB The maximum size of the contents of a deployment package, including layers and custom runtimes. (unzipped)'. 'Function layers | 5 layers'. The one aggregate number is code storage: 'Storage for uploaded functions (.zip file archives) and layers using Lambda-managed storage ... 300 GB (unzipped) | Not increasable.'

retention.stated: until the instance is recycled; not persistent

egress.terms: Not free and not public. Layer download is a signed S3 URL obtainable only via an authenticated `GetLayerVersion` call; there is no anonymous URL surface at all. Lambda invocations also bill per request and GB-second.

tooling: AWS CLI `publish-layer-version` / `get-layer-version`; SDKs. Immutability is structural: a layer version is immutable once published, so every write is a new version. No rclone backend.
chaining: 300 GB unzipped per region across functions + layers, non-increasable, is the only aggregate — so the whole region is a 300 GB bucket with a private API in front. 250 MB per layer, 5 layers per function, 50 MB per uploaded zip means the 250 MB ceiling can only be reached via S3-referenced uploads.
limits_note: 50 MB zipped via API/console; 250 MB unzipped total including layers and custom runtimes; 5 layers per function; 512 MB to 10,240 MB /tmp (ephemeral, per execution environment, dies with the environment); 300 GB regional code storage. Layers are immutable and versioned.

reliability_note: Very durable while the function exists; deleting a function version or layer version removes the code. No silent expiry, but no public read path either — the 300 GB is real and effectively unreachable without building your own proxy.
